I also agree with Shaggy and ThreeShem.

Good gimmick, but there's a critical lack of substance. Honestly, it feels more like the monologue a villain gives just before the heroes beat them than any grand analysis of the Foundation or the "unfair" treatment to a bit of programming that's apparently gone Skynet on the Foundation.

Basically, its stuff we've generally seen before without anything new on it beyond the "dialogue menu" style collapsibles.

item.content:encoded:
I understand you have feelings about the piece, but in general, saying "Look at how popular/highly ranked it is, therefore it must be of good quality." isn't a proper argument/defense.

There are plenty of low-quality works that become popular anyways.

There are plenty of mostly good things that have flaws that, if fixed, could make them better.

Rather than point at the ranking and say "but the rating!", consider the critiques, especially if you hear the same one multiple times, and see if there's something you're not seeing that could be fixed.

I’m in with Shaggy; this story has a good hook and an interesting gimmick, but we don’t get anything substantial meatwise from the story.

Some deep foundation secrets being revealed by the AI, maybe a conspiracy of some sort. Maybe the arc goes further down the path of releasing it; right now the story feels like that storyline got chopped before it could get started.

Right now, it’s just kind of a short, inconsequential conversation with GlaDos.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I don't think I've ever come across an SCP where the assumed reader is a civillian (closest I can recall is Jekeled's [sadly] self-deleted SCP wherein the file was captured documentation in the possession of Serpent's Hand members), so for that, this gets bonus points for having a decent level of originality.

While the basic idea is something I can totally get behind, the execution leaves much to be desired. It's all so very shallow - a brief overview of what the Foundation is, delivered through annoyingly short bursts - it's quite irritating to have the level of interaction limited essentially to nodding every couple of seconds.

I'd love to see another approach to this that goes a little more above and beyond in terms of substance. In its current state, there's nothing here to maintain intrigue. It feels like a waste of a good idea, having nothing to it in terms of actual content. -1
